transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer billing services. My name is Craig. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Craig. I opened my monthly mobile phone bill this morning and found a shocking forty-five pound extra charge listed as 'Maritime Satellite Roaming Data', even though I have an unlimited EU roaming add-on on my contract! I was taking the Irish Sea overnight ferry from Holyhead to Dublin on Thursday night, not a luxury Caribbean cruise!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly review those roaming billing records with you, Xander. Before we examine your itemized invoice, may I please verify your billing address and your security question answer?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 19 Montgomery Way, Chester, CH1 4NP. And my security question answer is my mother's birthplace, Inverness.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Xander, that verifies your account file. What mobile telephone number does this bill relate to?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is my main mobile number, 07700 900318. I am furious because forty-five pounds for thirty megabytes of background email syncing while asleep in a ferry cabin is absolute daylight robbery!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand your frustration upon seeing an unexpected forty-five pound charge on your monthly statement, Xander. Let us pull up the itemized call records and see exactly how those satellite data packets were billed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Craig, I appreciate you looking into it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So if I have understood correctly, you incurred a forty-five pound maritime satellite data roaming fee while traveling across the Irish Sea on an overnight ferry, which conflicts with your understanding of your inclusive EU roaming package, and you are seeking clarification and a fee adjustment. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly the issue. Ireland is in the European Union, so surely crossing to Dublin is covered under EU roaming!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looking at the billing timestamp on Thursday at 02:14 AM, your phone connected to 'Telenor Maritime' cellular satellite base station on board the vessel.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I never selected Telenor Maritime! My phone was sitting on the cabin bedside table in airplane mode... or at least I thought it was.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When a ferry travels twelve nautical miles off the coast into international waters, terrestrial UK and Irish cellular masts lose line-of-sight signal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And the ferry turns on its own mobile tower?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The ship operates an onboard satellite picocell relaying traffic over geostationary satellites, which falls under international maritime satellite bands rather than EU terrestrial roaming.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why isn't that made crystal clear when you purchase an EU roaming add-on?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our EU Roaming pass covers ground-based terrestrial mobile networks within EU Zone 1 countries, but explicitly excludes maritime, aerospace, and satellite networks.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Did S-Net send any text message warning me that maritime satellite rates applied?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated SMS gateway sent a welcome notification to your handset at 01:48 AM stating: 'Welcome to Maritime Network. Data is charged at £1.50 per megabyte'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: At two in the morning I was fast asleep! How can a sleeping passenger respond to an SMS?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I recognize that SMS alerts arriving during sleeping hours cannot be reviewed immediately, Xander.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly! My iPhone automatically downloaded email headers and weather updates in the background.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thirty megabytes of background data at one pound fifty per megabyte calculated to forty-five pounds before the automated spend cap paused the session.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can S-Net waive this charge as a one-off goodwill gesture? I have been a loyal customer for five years and never had a satellite roaming charge in my life.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can submit a billing adjustment request to our Roaming Operations team to review the wholesale interconnect fee with Telenor Maritime.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will they credit the forty-five pounds back to my account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The operations team reviews whether first-time maritime roaming thresholds qualify for a 50% or 100% courtesy waiver within five business days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That would be very helpful. Can you also put a permanent bar on satellite roaming on my SIM card?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I can activate our 'Terrestrial Only Roaming Bar' on your profile, which completely blocks maritime and aerospace satellite connections while preserving EU roaming.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please turn that bar on immediately so this can never happen on my return ferry.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Terrestrial Only Roaming Bar has now been applied to your SIM card and updates on the network within two hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That gives me much greater confidence for future ferry travel.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also look at your device settings to prevent background data roaming leaks in transit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Where on the iPhone should I adjust those settings?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open Settings, tap Mobile Service, tap Mobile Data Options, and toggle 'Low Data Mode' to ON.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Settings... Mobile Data Options... Low Data Mode is now toggled ON.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Low Data Mode halts automated iCloud backups, photo syncs, and background email fetches unless connected to WiFi.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is extremely useful protection for international travel.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check your monthly roaming spend cap setting on our customer portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What is my current monthly roaming spend cap set to?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your account defaulted to the standard forty-five pound regulatory spend cap, which is why your data stopped precisely at forty-five pounds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we reduce that cap to ten pounds so any accidental roaming is halted much sooner?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have adjusted your international roaming spend cap to ten pounds per billing cycle.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, that provides a tight safety net.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On future overnight ferry crossings, you can also purchase the ferry operator's passenger WiFi voucher directly, which provides flat-rate satellite internet without involving cellular networks.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, Irish Ferries offers an eight-pound overnight cabin WiFi pass. I will definitely use that instead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously that confirms your handset will automatically refuse connection to non-terrestrial shipboard cells in future, Xander.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Excellent. Now what about this current month's Direct Debit?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have placed a temporary twenty-day payment hold on the disputed forty-five pound portion so your bank account is not debited pending the review.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, that prevents an overdraft on my current account.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Which ferry crossing route did you take when this maritime charge occurred?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Craig, I told you in my very first sentence that I took the ferry from Holyhead to Dublin! Why are you asking me that again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I apologize, Xander, I wanted to double-check the port of departure for the operational ticket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, Holyhead to Dublin. Make sure you don't forget it on the ticket.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have recorded Holyhead to Dublin on the escalation record.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good. But I have to say, I am still not satisfied that S-Net allows these predatory satellite operators to charge £1.50 a megabyte without requiring active opt-in consent! It feels deceptive.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The maritime interconnect rates are determined under international maritime satellite treaties.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Regardless of treaties, customers should receive an explicit popup warning before a single kilobyte is billed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have noted your customer feedback regarding opt-in prompts on the policy feedback log.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, feedback or not, I still do not agree with this forty-five pound bill and I do not consider this issue resolved until that charge is credited off my statement!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The investigation team will email you within five working days with their decision. Have a good day. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
